questions.question: Applications connect to a storage account by using key1. You must regenerate key1 without causing an outage. What should you do first?

options.text: Update the applications to use key2
options.why: Correct. Move every client to the other key before you regenerate key1.

options.text: Regenerate key2
options.why: Regenerating key2 does not help the applications that use key1.

options.text: Set a key expiration policy
options.why: The policy only flags old keys. It does not prepare the applications.

options.text: Disable storage account key access
options.why: This breaks the applications immediately.

questions.explanation: Two keys allow rotation without downtime: switch clients to the other key, then regenerate the one no longer in use.

questions.question: You configure a key expiration policy of 90 days on a storage account. Which statement is true?

options.text: Keys older than 90 days are flagged as due for rotation, but they are not regenerated automatically
options.why: Correct. The policy provides reminders and compliance reporting only.

options.text: Both keys are regenerated automatically every 90 days
options.why: Azure does not rotate the keys for you.

options.text: Requests signed with a key older than 90 days are rejected
options.why: Old keys continue to work.

options.text: SAS tokens expire after 90 days
options.why: The key expiration policy does not set SAS expiry.

questions.explanation: Automate rotation with your own process, for example a script that updates Key Vault.

questions.question: A user is assigned the Reader role on a storage account and reports that the access keys are not visible. You must allow the user to view and regenerate the keys without granting other management permissions. Which role should you assign?

options.text: Storage Account Key Operator Service Role
options.why: Correct. It allows listing and regenerating keys only.

options.text: Owner
options.why: Owner grants full management access, which exceeds the requirement.

options.text: Storage Blob Data Reader
options.why: This is a data role and does not grant access to keys.

options.text: Reader and Data Access
options.why: This role allows viewing keys, but not regenerating them.

questions.explanation: Listing and regenerating keys require the listKeys and regenerateKey actions, which the Storage Account Key Operator Service Role includes.

questions.question: You regenerate key1 of a storage account. Which two items stop working? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Connection strings that contain the old key1
options.why: Correct. They are signed with a key that no longer exists.

options.text: Service SAS tokens that were signed with key1
options.why: Correct. Their signatures can no longer be verified.

options.text: User delegation SAS tokens
options.why: These are signed with a user delegation key from Microsoft Entra ID, not an account key.

options.text: Applications that use a managed identity with a Storage Blob Data role
options.why: Microsoft Entra ID authorization does not use account keys.

questions.explanation: Anything signed with the regenerated key fails. Entra ID access and user delegation SAS tokens are not affected.

questions.question: All applications that use a storage account now authenticate by using managed identities. You must prevent any future use of the account keys and of SAS tokens signed with them. What should you configure?

options.text: Set Allow storage account key access to Disabled
options.why: Correct. Shared Key requests, account SAS and service SAS are then refused.

options.text: Regenerate both keys
options.why: The new keys could still be used.

options.text: Create a key expiration policy of 1 day
options.why: The policy only flags old keys.

options.text: Set the minimum TLS version to 1.2
options.why: TLS settings do not affect key-based authorization.

questions.explanation: Disabling Shared Key authorization leaves Microsoft Entra ID and user delegation SAS as the only ways in.
